microsoft-password-spray.section: Password spray activity from CovertNetwork-1658 infrastructure
microsoft-password-spray.anchor: a very small number of sign-in attempts to many accounts
microsoft-password-spray.publisher_paraphrase: Microsoft reports very few sign-in attempts per account across many accounts. In about 80 percent of its reported cases there was one attempt per account per day. These are observations about the publisher's campaigns.
microsoft-password-spray.analyst_comparison: A local multi-account failure burst can be compared at the level of account distribution. That comparison does not establish the same actor, credential, IOC, campaign or compromise on local hosts.

redcanary-mshta.section: Detection opportunities / MSHTA spawning from suspect processes
redcanary-mshta.anchor: can be a good indicator of malice
redcanary-mshta.publisher_paraphrase: Red Canary identifies mshta.exe spawning powershell.exe or cmd.exe as a potential indicator of malice and a starting point for detection.
redcanary-mshta.analyst_comparison: Use this external detection lead to investigate process lineage; assess the local command and telemetry independently. The lead does not prove local download, C2 or compromise.

redcanary-mshta.anchor: At a minimum, collect parent-child process relationships
redcanary-mshta.publisher_paraphrase: Red Canary recommends collecting parent-child process relationships, with grandparent relationships where possible, as useful visibility for detecting adversary use of MSHTA.
redcanary-mshta.analyst_comparison: Process-creation visibility is distinct from successful command completion, output and service state in a local investigation.

uptycs-regsvr32.anchor: Threat actors can use regsvr32 for loading COM scriptlets
uptycs-regsvr32.publisher_paraphrase: Uptycs describes regsvr32 loading COM scriptlets as Squiblydoo and gives an example containing /s /n /u, an HTTP /i argument and scrobj.dll.
uptycs-regsvr32.analyst_comparison: The technique description provides background for investigating local scriptlet command arguments. An external example does not establish local transfer completion or confirmed C2.

uptycs-regsvr32.section: Insights From Our Threat Intelligence Systems
uptycs-regsvr32.anchor: provides telemetry with parent/child process relationships
uptycs-regsvr32.publisher_paraphrase: Uptycs describes its EDR telemetry with parent-child process relationships, correlation and threat intelligence for suspicious regsvr32 execution.
uptycs-regsvr32.analyst_comparison: Local process/network attribution still requires its own host, GUID, lifetime and destination evidence. A connection alone does not establish transmitted content, bytes or C2 purpose.
